description: The plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several Large Language Model (LLM) variants, including a baseline “Vanilla” model and multiple configurations of the proposed “SepLLM” and “StrmLLM” methods, as described in the paper “SepLLM: Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator.” The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from 0 to 140,000 with major tick marks at intervals of 20,000, and uses a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 with tick marks every 0.1 unit, also on a linear scale. Six distinct lines are plotted: “Vanilla” (purple, solid line) begins near 3.4 and declines steadily to approximately 2.5 by 140,000 iterations; “StrmLLM (n=64)” (blue, solid line) starts slightly below 3.4 and converges to about 2.6; “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange, solid line) follows a similar trajectory to StrmLLM, ending near 2.55; “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green, solid line) begins at 3.4 and decreases to roughly 2.53; “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red, solid line) starts at 3.4 and ends near 2.52; and “SepLLM (n=128)” (dark blue, solid line) begins at 3.4 and converges to approximately 2.6. All lines exhibit a steep initial drop in loss within the first 20,000 iterations, followed by a slower, gradual decline toward convergence. The legend is positioned in the upper right corner, and a light gray grid aids in reading values across the plot.
